newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk to restructure IPP contracts. [CORRECTED 14:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk to restructure IPP contracts. [CORRECTED 14:25 GMT]

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp and 16 regional independent power producers (IPP) said on Thursday they signed a restructuring agreement to terminate or restructure 29 IPP contracts representing more than 80 percent of Niagara's above market IPP costs. (Corrects percentages).
In exchange for terminating or restructuring these contracts, the IPPs will receive approximately $3.6 billion in cash and 46 million shares of Niagara stock.
Niagara and certain IPPs will also enter into restructured financial and physical contracts on terms more favorable to the company than the existing contracts.
The transaction is expected to reduce electricity prices for Niagara customers and help expedite competition.

This restructuring agreement formalizes a previously announced agreement between Niagara and 19 developers representing 44 contracts. Since the previous agreement, Niagara withdrew its offer with respect to a subgroup of three developers representing 15 hydro contracts with whom Niagara hopes to settle separately.

William Davis, chairman and chief executive officer of Niagara, said in a statement, "We are replacing a large and growing financial commitment with a defined debt obligation. The improved cash flow we expect to realize should allow us to begin immediately to reduce that debt."
"We seek to rebuild shareholder value, reduce prices for our customers and implement our plans to create a competive power market for New York electricity consumers," Davis concluded.
Niagara is an upstate New York electric and gas utility.
